newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian power firm sees little changed 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Croatian power firm sees little changed 1996 net.

text.p: Croatia's state power utility HEP said on Monday it expected a net profit of roughly 53 million kuna this year, little changed from last year's 53.5 million.
"This was a year of complete financial consolidation," board director Damir Begovic told reporters.
HEP used its entire 1995 proceeds to rebuild damaged infrastructure and Begovic said it would press on with the reconstruction of the supply and distribution network.
Next year would also see preparations for the overhaul of what he described as "capital energy facilities".
Last summer HEP reached tentative deals with U.S. corporations Enron and Enserch to finance the building three new power plants at over $1 billion.
To expand its production facilities, it also agreed with Germany's RWE to jointly complete another coal-powered thermal plant.
Croatia's electricity consumption, now at some 12.5 terraWatt-hours, is estimated to rise at an annual five percent. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
